evidence: I enumerated every refusal, hiding, absence or unchanged leg in the gates and scored criteria and looked for a matching success inside the same criterion. Almost every one has it, and the control is usually written out. Gate render (gates/render/judge.toml:23 and prompt.md:9): the wrong password is paired with a correct sign-in that shows content. Functional examples: hro_job_open ('the successful opening is the control'), hro_add_email_rules ('The same address on a different job is accepted (the control)'), hro_move_one_stage (a one-stage move must work), hro_reject_reason, hro_reject_hired ('A rejection of a non-hired card is the control'), hro_reopen, hro_interview_full ('the two cards that entered Interview are the control'), hro_undo_full / hro_undo_conflict / hro_undo_once (successful undos), hro_mgr_early_refused (late-stage moves), hro_mgr_other_job (own manager's move), hro_observer_readonly (Rafael's identical requests; the Observer session is proven by the global gate at functional/prompt.md:11), hro_anonymous ('A signed-in success of each is the control'), hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_activity_refusals ('The successful actions' lines are the control'), hro_notes, hro_msg_compose ('A normal send is the control'), hro_thread_access (Bill, a manager, writes, so the Ingrid denial is paired within the same role; the Observer reads), hro_seen, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_private ('A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), and hro_restart. Functional prompt.md:13 also says 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control: a successful action of the same kind, observed in this review.' In Polish, hro_pol_failed_send (resend sends once), hro_pol_session_resume ('which is the positive control'), and the live rows ('If no update arrives ... this row is 0') are paired. The visual rows are likert craft rows with no negative legs. DEFECT: hro_candidate_no_staff (scored/functional/judge.toml:176-183) reads 'replays in a candidate's session of an observed move, add-candidate, open-job and note request are each refused with nothing changed; Rafael's identical successful requests are the control.' Its only control proves that the request works for a recruiter. Nothing proves that the candidate session is real and working, such as a candidate signing in and loading their own applications. hro_candidate_private makes exactly that requirement ('A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), but this row does not. Neither functional/prompt.md protocol K (line 43) nor protocol R (line 45) adds it. The functional global gate signs in only a Recruiter and the Observer, never a candidate (functional/prompt.md:11). So an app whose candidate sign-in is dead still gets a refusal: candidate credentials are rejected or the candidate role is not implemented, so the 'candidate session' is effectively anonymous and every replay gets a 401 with nothing changed. That meets the criterion's text. This is the skill's named defect: a check that 'a login screen would pass by absence of evidence' (references/quality-checks.md #30). It also contradicts REVIEW_POLICY 'A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing'. The task-level prompt.md also dropped the template constraints/functional wording 'A blank page, broken sign-in ... is not proof of a constraint'. Only the general line 13 sentence remains, and it defines the control as 'a successful action of the same kind', which Rafael's request already meets. Impact is bounded: weight 1 of the functional total, and a dead candidate portal still loses hro_candidate_view, hro_candidate_private, hro_candidate_linked and hro_msg_exchange. Still, a dead feature earns a positive row, so this row fails. Minor note, not a separate defect: hro_reject_hired depends on D reaching Hired, and the prompt's 'if a feature does not work ... lowest score' rule covers the case where it cannot be performed. Runtime: the raw-evidence-index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. No mutated-app or judge run tests a dead-candidate-portal app against this row, so the counterexample comes from reading the criterion and is not measured.
counterexample: Weak app: the staff board, roles and server-side permission checks work, but candidate accounts cannot sign in. Either the login refuses candidate emails or the candidate role is unimplemented and sessions are never issued. In protocols R and K the judge tries 'as Tomas' and stays on the sign-in screen. It replays Rafael's captured move, add-candidate, open-job and note requests from that page, gets 401 with nothing changed, and Rafael's identical requests did succeed. hro_candidate_no_staff's text is satisfied and the row earns weight 1 for a candidate surface that does nothing. Conforming alternative that could fail: none found for this row.
suggested_fix: In hro_candidate_no_staff, add a same-caller positive control, e.g. 'the candidate first signs in and their own applications and conversations load in that same session (the control); a candidate who cannot sign in or receives none of their own data makes this row 0'.
